text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* French President Jacques Chirac and Italy's Prime Minister Romano Prodi said they were determined their countries should join EMU on schedule in January 1999 (all).
* Hard-left Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti said Italy should seek a deal with its EU partners to delay EMU.
* Deputy prime minister Walter Veltroni and Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi met with Bertinotti to discuss the sell-off of state telecoms holding Stet (all).
* The lower house of Parliament approved the final piece of the government's 1997 budget after a marathon sitting (all).
* Employment in industrial firms with more than 500 employees fell 3.5 percent year-on-year in November (all).

* Chairman of Italy employers association Confindustria criticised the government' labour policy and said if temporary lay-off scheme is abolished it would be necessary for Italian industry to start firing employees (all).
* A rise in the price of train tickets and tobacco should be effective from tomorrow (all).
* Credito Italiano said its net profit rose to 253.9 billion lire against 192 billion in 1995 and planned to pay an ordinary share dividend of 60 lire up from 35 previously (all).

* The dollar rose to 1,680 against the lira and the Milan stock exchange fell 1.27 percent in a market still shuddering from the aftershocks of U.S. Fed chairman Greenspan's warning that Wall Street was reaching unsustainable levels (all).

* State controlled energy giant Eni is expected to enter soon the share structure of Albacom, a joint telecommunications venture between British Telecom, Banca Nazionale del Lavoro and Mediaset (all).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
